symbol_repair_2026_11_07.method: in-place repair, not a reconversion: pua_map_inplace.py (kept outside the repository) maps the Symbol-font private-use code points U+F0A3, U+F0B3 and U+F0B4 to ≤, ≥ and × and changes no other byte. The deposit's converter (epub_text of the workbench's harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py as it was on 2026-10-23) was not rerun: it has since been changed (from 2026-10-24 it keeps paragraphs inside table cells), so a reconversion would change far more than the symbols.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.previous_converter: workbench harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py (epub_text), the converter of the 2026-10-23 deposit
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.checked_against: the Register's current Word rendering of the Guide (F2016L01332, volume 2, .docx), which has the same characters as Symbol-font private-use code points (18 x U+F0A3, 18 x U+F0B3, 5 x U+F0B4, each in a run in the Symbol font)
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: The EPUB carries characters typed in the Symbol font as raw private-use code points (U+F0xx), which epub_text kept as they were; they display as empty boxes.

A diff against the previous deposit shows no other change.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.not_restored: The Word original has 18 ≤ and 18 ≥; the other 6 of each are row and column labels in table cells of the hearing-loss scales that epub_text dropped altogether with the cells around them (see text_caveat). They are not symbol losses and are not restored here.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: the subject has no encodings; the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986 baseline (vea-guide.l4) reads only Table 23.1 from F2016L01332.tables.md and relies on none of the changed lines
